subject: Clarification: Multi-region DR RPO exclusion & ownership split
messages:
From: Elena Cortez <elena.cortez@pendulumpay.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Contracts <contracts@pendulumpay.com>
Date: 2028-06-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Multi-region DR: question on RPO carve-out language

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the call this morning. As we work through Procurement and Legal, there's a specific ask from our Ops team: explicitly call out an RPO exclusion in the DR section for certain archival tiers during multi-region failover scenarios.

Essentially: if a failover requires restoring from cold archival snapshots (cold-tier data >30 days), Pendulum needs to accept a longer RPO for that subset and that should not count toward uptime SLAs. Legal wants short, contract-friendly language and a clear set of triggers/conditions.

Can Redwood provide proposed contract wording and an operational acceptance matrix (how long activation takes, who owns restore steps, expected credit structure if activation exceeds lead times)?

If easier, loop in whoever owns runbook / reliability so we have an operational anchor.

Thanks — happy to chat if anything is ambiguous.

Elena Cortez
Director, Site Reliability
Pendulum Payments

attachment: pendulum_dr_questions.xlsx (XLSX)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Elena Cortez <elena.cortez@pendulumpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-25T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Multi-region DR: question on RPO carve-out language

Elena — appreciate the clear ask. Looping in Marissa for contracting & credits and Karthik/Mina for runbook and risk specifics.

High-level proposal from Redwood:
- Contract clause: "In the event of a declared multi-region failover where customer data requires restoration from Cold Archive (defined as object age > 30 days or explicitly identified archival buckets), Redwood will have an agreed extended RPO for that archival subset of up to 72 hours. Such extended RPOs will be scoped to the archival subset and are excluded from the calculation of platform availability and uptime SLAs for the affected period."
- Operational triggers:
  * Trigger = cross-region outage declared by Redwood OR customer-requested region switch where primary region data is unavailable.
  * Archival eligibility = objects marked archival or >30 days since last active write.
- Ownership: Redwood will perform restoration orchestration; customer maintains final data validation and rehydration acceptance.
- Credits: For archival restores that exceed agreed lead times (see attached matrix), a modest usage credit or service credit can be offered; exceptions for major disasters will have alternate remediation (post-event review + credit at Redwood discretion).

Karthik / Mina — can you review and supply a short ops annex (lead times, step owners, estimated timeline for cold restore) and confirm whether 72 hours is a feasible safety valve?

Marissa — I flagged this as an open concession we may need to trade for a 9-12 month committed seat in Dedicated. Thoughts on commercial offset?

Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

attachment: proposed-sla-clause-draft.txt (TXT)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Elena Cortez <elena.cortez@pendulumpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-26T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Multi-region DR: question on RPO carve-out language

Elena / team — quick technical note and proposed annex text.

Short answer: 72 hours as a contractual maximum for cold-archive subsets is reasonable provided we define narrow eligibility and SLAs layered by storage class. Operational caveats:
- If objects were evicted from hot/warm cache and require full rehydration from third-party cold storage (customer-managed archive or long-term blob tier), the restore timeline is dominated by the archive provider (we'll need a cross-reference).
- Practical restore flow:
  1) Declare failover + identify archival buckets (t0).
  2) Redwood submits batch rehydration jobs + pre-warms KV caches for indexes (t0 + 2–6 hours).
  3) Progressive rehydration; most critical keys available within 12–36 hours depending on data volume.
  4) Full cold restore completion target: 72 hours for standard volumes (defined as <= 50TB archival object set).

Annex wording suggestion (ops): "Redwood will initiate restoration and rehydration processes within 2 hours of a declared multi-region failover. For archival subsets (objects designated archival or >30 days since last write), expected rehydration to prioritized service tiers is progressive with a contractual maximum of 72 hours for archival subsets up to 50TB. Restoration timelines for larger volumes or where third-party cold storage egress limits apply will be handled per the attached DR-risk-acceptance-matrix and may be subject to additional review."

I attached an excerpted ops runbook and a small matrix that maps archival size bands to expected timelines and ownership (see attachments).

Karthik Iyer
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

attachment: ops-runbook-excerpt.txt (TXT)

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Elena Cortez <elena.cortez@pendulumpay.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Contracts <contracts@pendulumpay.com>
Date: 2028-06-26T14:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Multi-region DR: question on RPO carve-out language

Thanks — I've attached the DR-risk-acceptance-matrix and a proposed responsibility split. A few operational clarifications to make the contract clean:

- Narrow the scope: archival RPO exclusion applies only when (a) affected objects are in archival storage classes OR (b) the customer explicitly flags a dataset as "archival-exempt" in an attachment to the contract.
- Escalation: Redwood will provide continuous restore progress and a runbook point-of-contact. If restore progress stalls beyond the size-banded thresholds, an on-call postmortem and joint remediation plan will be executed.
- Credit structure: For archival restores that overrun the banded timeline (not in catastrophic regionwide loss that prevents egress), proposed remedial credit = 5% of monthly usage for every 24-hour block over threshold, capped at 30% for the incident.

Please note Legal may want slightly different phrasing; Contracts: if the above is acceptable operationally, please translate into simple legal language and return redlines.

Mina Haddad
Head of Reliability, Redwood Inference

attachments: DR-risk-acceptance-matrix.xlsx, proposed-responsibility-split.docx

From: Elena Cortez <elena.cortez@pendulumpay.com>

Cc: Contracts <contracts@pendulumpay.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-27T10:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Multi-region DR: question on RPO carve-out language

Mina / team — this is very helpful and gives us what Legal needs to draft. A few quick notes from Procurement:

- Pendulum accepts the archival carve-out with the following conditions:
  1) The 30-day archival threshold must be explicitly listed (we'll include a table of buckets).
  2) Credits above look reasonable; Procurement asks for a minimum service credit of 2% immediately after the first 24h overrun. The cap at 30% is acceptable.
  3) We want a standard clause that Redwood will notify us via email and the incident channel within 60 minutes of declaring a failover.

If Redwood can add the 60-minute notification window and the 2% immediate credit, we can push this through Legal this week. Once Contracts returns the redline, we'll route for signature.

Elena Cortez
Director, Site Reliability
Pendulum Payments
